model: Life insurer FCFE at cost of equity, net debt held at zero (engine route)

inputs.base_revenue_note: FY2025 total ADJUSTED revenues (premiums + policy charges + net investment income + asset-management fees/other, excluding realized gains, MRB changes and Divested/Run-off businesses): Q1 13,412 + Q2 13,506 + Q3 16,239 + Q4 14,520, from the Q2-2026 Quarterly Financial Supplement (8-K 2026-08-04, Ex 99.2, p.3). This is the revenue line adjusted operating income is earned on; the CSV's GAAP Revenue (60,774) includes realized gains/losses and run-off businesses. Premiums are lumpy (pension-risk-transfer single premiums), so revenue-based margins carry quarter noise; TTM to 30 June 2026 was 60,148.
inputs.share_count_basis: 348.9M end-of-period DILUTED common shares at 30 June 2026 (Q2-2026 earnings release, adjusted book value table). Cross-check: 345M basic outstanding at 31 July 2026 (10-Q cover) plus ~3.7M dilutive awards. Held FLAT: SBC is charged in the flows, and the $1.0bn/yr repurchase programme (2026 authorisation $1.0bn, $500M done by 30 June) is a use of the FCFE being capitalised, not extra growth.
inputs.net_debt_treatment: Held at ZERO. Total debt $20,618M at 30 June 2026 = capital debt $14,206M + operating debt $5,985M + limited/non-recourse $427M (QFS p.'Short-term and long-term debt'). Interest on capital debt sits inside Corporate & Other adjusted operating income (holdco net interest expense $595M in H1-2026), and operating debt is matched by the assets it funds, so the AOI-based flow is already post-financing; deducting debt again would count it twice. Consolidated cash ($15,162M at 30 June 2026) is general-account and policyholder liquidity, not surplus. Parent highly liquid assets of $4,200M (ex intercompany liquidity account) are treated as the required holdco buffer and NOT added -- conservative by perhaps $1-2bn ($3-6/share) if management regards part of it as excess.
inputs.last_fcf_note: FY2025 capital returned to common shareholders: dividends $1,932M + repurchases $1,000M (QFS distributions table). Used as the observed FCFE proxy = 57% of FY2025 after-tax AOI ($5,161M). Parent highly liquid assets fell $824M over FY2025 (4,641 -> 3,817) partly on net debt repayment, so organic FCFE was at or slightly below distributions; H1-2026 organic holdco cash generation (business capital activity $1,652M less net interest $595M, plus tax/other/affiliated operating flows) was ~$1.5bn = ~56% of H1 AOI. An insurer's OCF-less-capex is not free cash, so the owner-FCF identity last_fcf = reported_fcf - sbc - interest_income is deliberately not satisfied.
inputs.sbc_source: PRU_Metrics.csv StockBasedComp FY2025 $257M (SEC XBRL, cash-flow add-back); FY2024 $314M, FY2023 $254M. Award-settlement withholding is not separately disclosed and is immaterial against the $1bn buyback; charged at 0.45% of adjusted revenue.
inputs.buyback_note: Repurchases $1,000M in each of FY2023 (1,012), FY2024 and FY2025; $496M in H1-2026 (holdco sources/uses). Diluted count fell 359.3M (FY2024) -> 348.9M (Jun-26), ~1.9%/yr.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of EQUITY 10.0% (USD flows): 10-year UST ~4.3% + 5.0% ERP x beta ~1.15, rounded up. Half a point above the 9.5% used for MET because PRU carries the same rate/credit/equity sensitivity plus a live governance failure in its largest international unit (Prudential of Japan), a run-off legacy variable-annuity and GUL block, a five-year divestiture programme and a persistent gap between GAAP net income and AOI. It is a cost of equity, not a WACC, because the flows are post-interest FCFE. Same rate in all three scenarios; scenario risk sits in the driver paths and weights, not a stacked discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Not applicable: operating leases are immaterial for an insurer and their cost is already inside the AOI expense base.
inputs.nci_treatment: None in the flows or bridge: adjusted operating income EXCLUDES earnings attributable to noncontrolling and redeemable noncontrolling interests (benefits and expenses include a charge for them; Q2-2026 release, Non-GAAP Measures), so AOI is already attributable to PFI. NCI equity is $358M at 30 June 2026 and the NCI share of H1-2026 net income was $60M.
inputs.preferred_treatment: No preferred stock outstanding. The 4.125%/5.625%/5.950% junior subordinated notes (PFH/PRS/PRH) are debt; their interest is inside AOI.
inputs.notes: MODEL: FCFE at cost of equity on a diversified life insurer / asset manager, run through the component engine with net debt at zero -- the MET / GL / IAG.AX cost-of-equity-stream precedent. The dcf-methods routing default for an insurer is BVPS-compounding x exit P/B; overridden because (1) GAAP book is not a usable compounding base: LDTI restated equity from $63.7bn (FY2019) / $68.2bn (FY2020) to ~$30bn (FY2021 restated), and AOCI (-$4.1bn at 30 June 2026) moves billions with rates; (2) PRU does not compound book -- it distributes ~57% of AOI (~$2.9bn/yr, ~$1.9bn dividends + $1.0bn buybacks) and adjusted book per share grew only 4.7% in the year to June 2026 ($96.41 -> $100.91); the value driver is the cash the holding company can distribute. Using the same method as MET keeps the two directly comparable. EARNINGS ANCHOR: adjusted operating income, not GAAP net income. AOI is management's ASC 280 segment measure and strips out mark-to-market noise (market-risk-benefit changes, hedge marks, experience-rated contractholder pass-throughs) that is genuinely non-economic in any one year. But AOI also excludes real costs -- net credit-related losses (~$75M a quarter) and some realized losses on sales -- and GAAP NI has run persistently below it (FY2025 NI $3,732M vs AOI $5,161M; H1-2026 $1,582M vs $2,716M). That gap is handled by calibrating the FCFE conversion to ACTUAL holdco cash and capital returned (~57% of AOI), not to AOI itself, so whatever part of the GAAP-only losses is economic is already inside the conversion rate. ENGINE MAPPING: revenue = total adjusted revenues; ebitda_margin_path = pre-tax AOI BEFORE stock compensation as % of adjusted revenue (FY2025: (6,637 + 257) / 57,677 = 11.95%); sbc_pct_path 0.45%; da_pct_path 0 (D&A immaterial, no PP&E capex); cash_tax_rate_path 21.5% (AOI effective tax: FY2025 1,476/6,637 = 22.2%, H1-2026 737/3,453 = 21.3%), so (margin - SBC) x (1 - tax) = after-tax AOI; capex_pct_path = capital RETAINED in the insurance subsidiaries (statutory new-business strain, RBC/ESR growth, capital contributions, holdco costs, and the economic part of GAAP-only credit losses), set so FCFE = the scenario's free-cash-flow conversion of after-tax AOI. BVPS CROSS-CHECK: adjusted book value $100.91/share, GAAP BV $90.50, GAAP ex-AOCI $102.14 (30 June 2026). The $113.13 price is 1.12x adjusted book against a ~15% operating ROE (Q2-2026 TTM operating ROE 15.5% H1) but ~10-11% GAAP ROE; at a 10% cost of equity and 3% growth that brackets a justified P/B of ~1.1x (GAAP ROE) to ~1.7x (operating ROE). Capital: PICA RBC 415% at 31 Dec 2025 (10-Q liquidity section); Japanese subsidiaries now report ESR (first disclosure 31 March 2026); management does not expect a material capital, ESR or cash-flow impact from the Japan suspension (10-Q Company Overview).
inputs.japan_suspension_treatment: 10-Q (Q2-2026) Company Overview: the suspension cut International pre-tax AOI by an estimated $235M in H1-2026; full-year 2026 hit $525-575M, 2027 hit $400-450M (remediation, one-time costs, gradual ramp after sales resume); +$50-60M per month if the suspension runs past 5 Nov 2026. Base takes both years at the midpoints and assumes sales resume on schedule; bear extends the suspension ~4 months into 2027 and adds Gibraltar Life spillover; bull resumes on schedule with a faster ramp. No capital/cash impact assumed, per management.
inputs.strategy_overhaul_treatment: August 2026 plan: exit emerging markets (~6-7 country businesses, ~half the country footprint) over ~5 years, unlocking 'well north of $3bn' of capital; $750M of annual expense savings by year-end 2028 (~150bp expense-ratio improvement); PGIM toward ~25% of earnings; higher FCF conversion. Already in train: ICEA Lion (Kenya, 24%) and Indonesia JV (49%) sales signed, PGIM India sale to TVS Venu signed April 2026 -- all moved to Divested and Run-off (outside AOI). Treatment: (a) the DIVESTITURES are modelled as value-neutral in base -- the exited businesses' earnings stay in the flows and no proceeds are added, which is equivalent to selling them at the value this model places on them (~$3bn+ of capital released against what is likely a few hundred million of after-tax AOI, i.e. roughly the 10-13x FCFE multiple used here). Bull credits a premium through higher conversion; bear a discount through lower conversion. (b) COST SAVES enter the margin path, base taking roughly half of the $750M to the bottom line by FY2028 after reinvestment, legacy-VA run-off and PGIM fee pressure; bull takes ~all of it. (c) FCF CONVERSION rises in base from 57% to 63% by FY2030 as capital-hungry EM units leave; bull to 70%; bear flat at 55%.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: GAAP revenue 3yr CAGR 2.2% plus management's high-single-digit earnings-growth framework (ex legacy VA) haircut for run-off; equity CAGRs are broken by LDTI and AOCI
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR (-13.6%) is an accounting artefact: LDTI restated FY2021 equity from ~$63.7bn to ~$30bn and AOCI swings billions with rates. GAAP EPS 3yr/5yr CAGRs are undefined (FY2022 EPS -4.49, FY2020 -1.00); FY2023 -> FY2025 GAAP EPS went 6.76 -> 10.05. No owner-FCF series exists for an insurer (OCF less capex is not free cash), so FCF CAGRs are null.
historical_growth.notes: GAAP revenue (CSV) is volatile from PRT single premiums and realized gains: 57,033 (FY2020), 71,247 (FY2021), 56,881 (FY2022), 53,979 (FY2023), 70,405 (FY2024), 60,774 (FY2025). Adjusted revenue FY2025 57,677; TTM Jun-26 60,148. After-tax AOI FY2025 5,161 (Q1 1,188 / Q2 1,284 / Q3 1,521 / Q4 1,168); H1-2026 2,716 vs H1-2025 2,472 (+10%) despite the Japan drag; AOI EPS H1-2026 $7.69 vs $6.87.

base.narrative: FY2026: adjusted revenue +3.2% (H1 29,389 +9%, H2 normalising after the Q3-2025 PRT spike); pre-tax AOI ~$6.7bn = H1 $3,453M + H2 ~$3.27bn, the H2 carrying ~$315M of the $525-575M Japan hit and the Corporate & Other loss to the guided $1.55bn -> after-tax ~$5.3bn, ~$15.2 per diluted share. FY2027: Japan drag eases to $400-450M and cost saves start (margin 12.1%). FY2028-29: Japan normal, roughly half the $750M saves retained after reinvestment, legacy VA run-off and PGIM fee compression, margin 12.4-12.5% (after-tax AOI ~$6.0bn FY2028, ~6-7%/yr per-share growth before buybacks -- below management's high-single-digit framework). FCF conversion 57% (FY2026, = FY2025 actual) rising to 63% by FY2030 as EM capital is released; divestitures value-neutral. Terminal min(Gordon 10%/2.5%, 13x FCFE).

bull.narrative: Japan sales resume 5 Nov 2026 and ramp quickly (2027 drag at the low end); the full $750M of savings reaches the bottom line by 2028; PGIM margin keeps expanding (+200bp in 2026, 28.2% in Q2) and PGIM moves toward 25% of earnings; retail annuity (RILA) and PRT/longevity flow sustain 4.5-5% revenue growth. Margin to 13.5% (after-tax AOI ~10.2% of revenue, near the top of PRU's post-LDTI range). EM exits close at a premium and free capital-hungry units, lifting conversion from 58% to 70% by FY2030. Terminal min(Gordon 10%/3%, 14x).

bear.narrative: The Japan suspension runs ~4 months past November (+$200-240M pre-tax in 2027 at the disclosed $50-60M/month), reputational damage spreads to Gibraltar Life's channel, and Japanese in-force runs off faster. Rates fall and spreads compress on Retirement; a credit cycle hits PGIM private credit flows; cost saves are absorbed by remediation and run-off. Margin dips to 11.4% in FY2027 and stays at 11.5% (below FY2025's 11.95%). EM businesses sell below value or slowly, so conversion stays at 55% (below the 57% delivered). Terminal min(Gordon 10%/2%, 11x).

scenario_narratives.base: A US-centred life, retirement and asset-management franchise working through a bad year in Japan. AOI absorbs a ~$550M pre-tax Japan hit in 2026 and ~$425M in 2027, then recovers; half the $750M cost programme sticks; conversion of AOI into distributable cash edges up from 57% to 63% as emerging-market units are sold at roughly what they are worth. That is worth more than the price at a 10% cost of equity, and most of the gap comes from the market applying a GAAP-earnings (not AOI) multiple and a governance discount.
scenario_narratives.bull: The strategic reset works as pitched: Japan resumes on schedule, the full cost programme drops through, PGIM grows toward a quarter of earnings, and the EM exits release more than $3bn at premium prices into a business that converts 70% of earnings to cash. PRU re-rates toward MET.
scenario_narratives.bear: Japan proves a longer and wider governance problem, the divestiture programme drags or sells cheaply, and lower rates and a credit cycle compress spreads and PGIM flows. Earnings stall near today's level and conversion stays in the mid-50s.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%: the Japan suspension has already been extended once, the regulator's response is open, the 10-Q itself flags possible spillover to Gibraltar Life, and a leveraged spread balance sheet has asymmetric downside in a rate-and-credit downturn. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs several independent things to happen together -- on-time Japan resumption with a fast ramp, the full $750M of saves, EM sales at premium prices, and a 70% conversion rate PRU has not delivered. Same 25/50/25 as MET, the closest comparable.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value PRU on the cash its holding company can actually return to shareholders (FCFE), discounted at a 10% cost of equity with debt held inside the flows. Earnings are built from adjusted operating income -- the right measure of what the businesses earn in a year -- but the cash conversion is set to what PRU has actually distributed (~57% of AOI), so the AOI-to-GAAP gap is priced in rather than ignored. The two live events, the Prudential of Japan suspension and the August 2026 emerging-markets exit and cost programme, are modelled explicitly using management's own disclosed figures, haircut in base and stressed in bear. Adjusted book ($100.91) and operating ROE (~15%) are a cross-check, not the driver.
key_risks_to_valuation: Prudential of Japan: suspension extended past 5 Nov 2026 costs $50-60M pre-tax per month; regulatory penalties or spillover to Gibraltar Life are not in base
Divestiture execution: the >$3bn capital unlock is treated as value-neutral; selling below value or slowly destroys value the base case does not subtract
Interest rates and spreads: Retirement and International spread income are rate-sensitive in both directions; legacy VA/GUL blocks carry equity-market and policyholder-behaviour risk
Earnings quality: GAAP NI has run 25-45% below AOI (realized/credit losses, MRB marks); if more of that gap is economic, the 57% conversion is too high
Yen: Japan earnings and capital translate at the prevailing JPY/USD rate
PGIM flows: affiliated outflows (-$3.0bn in Q2-2026) and the industry shift away from active equity pressure fees
